title: Ethiopia
capsule: Modern Ethiopia — formally the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia — remained a sovereign state through the twentieth century except during the Italian occupation of 1936–1941; the dataset's from-year of 1942 reflects the post-liberation reconstitution under Haile Selassie I. The imperial era ended with the 1974 Derg coup that deposed Haile Selassie; a Marxist military dictatorship under Mengistu Haile Mariam (1977–1991) was in turn overthrown by the EPRDF coalition, which established a federal republic. Ethiopia remains the most populous landlocked country in the world and hosts the headquarters of the African Union (launched in 2002) in Addis Ababa, which had earlier been the founding seat of the AU's predecessor, the Organisation of African Unity, in 1963.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Ethiopia's borders are established by colonial-era treaties and are generally well-attested, though the Eritrean border remains disputed following the 1998–2000 war and subsequent arbitration.
